name: Teleportation consumes one ebit; entanglement cannot be restored by LOCC (called a 'conservation law')

source.located: Bennett, Brassard, Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres, Wootters, PRL 70, 1895 (1993) [teleportation; no arXiv copy]; Bennett, Bernstein, Popescu, Schumacher, PRA 53, 2046 (1996), quant-ph/9511030 [ebit consumption, non-increase of expected entanglement under local operations, asymptotic reversibility for pure states]; Nielsen, PRL 83, 436 (1999), quant-ph/9811053 [exact single-copy pure-state LOCC conversion iff majorization]; Horodecki^4, RMP 81, 865 (2009), quant-ph/0702225 [restatement of the 1993 protocol, eqs. (8)-(9); monotonicity axiom, eq. (150); 'separable cannot be transformed into entangled by LOCC at all', p.51]
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries: quant-ph/0702225 pp.4,11,12,51,57 (restates Bennett et al. 1993 exactly); quant-ph/9511030 pp.1-8,15-17 READ at source; quant-ph/9811053 pp.1-4 READ at source. The 1993 PRL itself is NAMED-NOT-READ (no arXiv copy); its content is taken from the Horodecki review's eq. (8)-(9) restatement and BBPS p.2 ('the consumption of one shared ebit, together with the transmission of a two-bit classical message, can be substituted for the transmission of one qubit').

published_statement: BBPS 1996 (quant-ph/9511030) p.2: 'In [4] [Bennett et al. 1993] ... it is shown that the consumption of one shared ebit, together with the transmission of a two-bit classical message, can be substituted for the transmission of one qubit.' p.6: 'neither the measurement of k nor any other local processing by one or both parties can increase the expected entropy of entanglement between Alice's and Bob's subsystems ... though Alice and Bob cannot by local actions increase their expected entanglement, they can gamble with it.' Abstract/p.16: concentration and dilution 'asymptotically conserve entropy of entanglement' for PURE states; for mixed states reversibility was unknown. p.15: teleporting C through singlets 'has the effect of destroying the entanglement between A and C while creating the desired entangled state Psi(A,B)'. Horodecki review (quant-ph/0702225) p.57 eq.(150): 'Monotonicity under LOCC: Entanglement cannot increase under local operations and classical communication', E(Lambda(rho)) <= E(rho); p.4: entanglement 'can not be increased on average when systems are not in direct contact'; p.51: 'In bipartite states we cannot transform separable state into entangled one by LOCC at all'; p.11: after teleportation 'Alice has just one of the Bell states: the systems A and A' becomes entangled after measurement, and no information about the state |q> is left with her.' Nielsen 1999 Thm 1: |psi> -> |phi> by LOCC iff lambda_psi majorized by lambda_phi (exact, deterministic, single copy, pure states; 'We do not consider approximate transformations').
published_hypotheses: teleportation (1993, as restated): an UNKNOWN qubit, one maximally entangled pair shared in advance, a Bell-basis measurement by Alice, two classical bits sent, a Pauli correction by Bob; fidelity 1 on every outcome
ebit accounting (BBPS): pure states; entropy of entanglement as the measure; the 'consumption of one ebit' is for faithful transmission of an arbitrary qubit

monotonicity (BBPS p.6; Horodecki eq.150): operations restricted to LOCC; for known measures the strong form holds only ON AVERAGE over outcomes (single outcomes can exceed the start -- the 'gamble'); the state-level form E(Lambda(rho)) <= E(rho) is the axiom
conservation/reversibility (BBPS abstract, p.16): ASYMPTOTIC (n -> infinity), PURE states only, with vanishing error; not known (1996) and since refuted in general for mixed states
Nielsen 1999: exact, deterministic, single-copy, pure-state LOCC conversions
hypothesis_drift: STRENGTHENED WORDING: transit.py:24-28, :213, :221, :283 call the consumption 'a CONSERVATION LAW rather than a design choice'. The sources state a NON-INCREASE (monotonicity) law, not conservation. Computed here (rederive part C): for a pure input qubit the entanglement across the Alice|Bob cut goes 1 -> 0 (destroyed; Alice's leftover Bell pair on AA' is local); only when the teleported qubit is itself half of an entangled pair R-A does the cut entanglement stay 1 -> 1 (moved to R-B, entanglement swapping). Conservation holds in the literature only asymptotically for pure states (BBPS) or with an entanglement battery (2405.10599); for mixed states entanglement manipulation is irreversible (2111.02438). This is a naming discrepancy: the channel-consumption conclusion does not depend on it.

DROPPED: exact fidelity. transit.py:27-28 ('You could not keep it open if you wanted to') and :221-222 ('you could not hold it open if you wanted to') are modal claims over all protocols; they hold only if the transfer is EXACT (F = 1). Computed (part E): measure-and-prepare leaves the pair untouched (E_after = 1) at average fidelity 2/3; consumption of the full ebit is forced only at F = 1 (part D). specthm.py:1186-1187 records for R11 that 'the fidelity is not yet fixed' while specthm.py:1209 binds CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE on it -- the consumption result binds R11 only at F = 1.

DROPPED (in transit.py; KEPT in specthm.py): the state is UNKNOWN/arbitrary. transit.py:24-28 and :151 state consumption unconditionally; specthm.py:1188-1190 (H_tele 'unknown quantum state') and :1212 ('A KNOWN state can be re-prepared rather than teleported, and then the channel is not consumed') carry the hypothesis. ledger.py M-S1A-P5 (:1357-1365) quotes CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE with no hypothesis.

DROPPED: resource is exactly one ebit (pure, maximally entangled, 2-dim). 'One pair, one transit' (transit.py:27, :219) is per ebit: computed (part D) a 2-ebit channel may teleport one qubit and keep one ebit; a channel with less than 1 ebit cannot teleport exactly at all (z3: p must equal 1/2).

DROPPED: deterministic, and 'cannot be restored' is ON AVERAGE for entangled starts (BBPS p.6 'gamble'); for the post-teleportation state specifically it is strict, because that state is a product across the cut (computed, part A) and LOCC cannot make separable states entangled (Horodecki p.51; part F). No drift in the conclusion the tree draws, but the tree states no hypothesis.

DECLARED, NOT COMPUTED: CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER = 0.0 (transit.py:139) is a constant, and the selftest (transit.py:339) compares the constant with 0.0 -- a tautology; the report's 'purity 1.000000000, pure' (transit.py:217) is a literal string. Computed here (part A, sympy exact): the post-measurement state factorises |Bell_m>_{AA'} (x) sigma_m|q>_B on every outcome, so E_after = 0 exactly and B's corrected state is |q> with purity 1 per outcome. The declared values AGREE with the computation; the drift is in status (declared), not in value. Without the 2 bits B is I/2 (not pure) -- transit.py itself shows this at :188-199; the purity-1 literal is true per outcome after correction only.
NO SOURCE NAMED: transit.py cites none of Bennett et al. 1993, BBPS 1996, Vidal 2000 or the Horodecki review for the ebit cost or the LOCC monotonicity (canonical entry hypothesis 3).

data_at_publication.source_now: rederive part A; exact, no measured datum

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0). A (sympy exact): Bell reduced entropy = 1; on all four outcomes the post-measurement state factorises AA'|B, so E_after = 0, and after Pauli correction B = |q> exactly. B: outcome-averaged state with Alice's record is PPT (N = -2.2e-16) and B without the bits is I/2. C: cut entanglement 1 -> 0 for a pure input (NOT conserved), 1 -> 1 for an entangled input (moved A'B -> RB); the channel pair itself is spent in both. D (z3, residual Schmidt dim 2,3,4, all unsat; vacuity guard sat): by Nielsen's theorem plus the teleport-half-of-a-local-Bell-pair reduction, a pure rank-2 channel that teleports an arbitrary qubit exactly and deterministically must be maximally entangled (p = 1/2) and leaves a product residual -- the ebit is wholly consumed; a 2-ebit channel may keep 1. E (sympy): dropping F = 1, measure-and-prepare leaves E_after = 1 at average fidelity 2/3. F: 2000 random Alice POVMs never raise the expected entropy of entanglement (max change -3.5e-4) but 559 single outcomes exceed the start (the BBPS 'gamble'); from the product post-teleportation state no LOCC outcome is entangled.

later_literature.ref: Lami & Regula, 'No second law of entanglement manipulation after all', arXiv:2111.02438 (Nature Physics 2023)
later_literature.what: Theorem 1: entanglement manipulation is irreversible even under all non-entangling operations; two-qutrit omega_3 has E_c = 1 > E_d = log2(3/2). There is no single conserved entropy-like quantity for mixed states -- the 'conservation law' wording in transit.py has no general counterpart; LOCC monotonicity (the tree's actual need) is untouched.

later_literature.ref: Ganardi, Kondra, Ng, Streltsov, 'Second Law of Entanglement Manipulation with Entanglement Battery', arXiv:2405.10599
later_literature.what: With an auxiliary battery whose entanglement must not decrease, conversions are reversible and governed by any additive measure (Thm 1, 2): a conservation-like law exists only in this enlarged setting. Their eq. (14) re-derives non-increase in the main system from additivity plus LOCC monotonicity. Note-added reports proofs of the generalized quantum Stein lemma restoring reversibility under asymptotically non-entangling operations (not LOCC). None of this lets LOCC alone restore a consumed ebit.

later_literature.ref: Nielsen, 'Conditions for a class of entanglement transformations', quant-ph/9811053
later_literature.what: Exact single-copy pure-state LOCC conversion iff majorization; used here (z3) to show exact teleportation consumes the whole ebit and needs a maximal channel. Later than 1993/1996, sharpens the ebit-cost statement to a single-shot theorem.

later_literature.ref: entanglement embezzlement literature surfaced by discover_papers (e.g. arXiv:2410.19051, 2509.15749, 2605.22713, 2609.26362)
later_literature.what: Embezzling states let local operations extract entanglement while perturbing a pre-shared resource arbitrarily little in trace distance. They require a large pre-existing entangled resource and are approximate; they do not contradict exact LOCC monotonicity and do not restore entanglement from a product state. Recorded as a boundary on how 'cannot be restored' may be read (approximate, with extra resource), not as a counterexample.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: the underlying results are theorems of finite-dimensional quantum mechanics under the LOCC restriction; no measured datum enters them, so there is no datum the 1993/1996 authors could have lacked that would move the conclusion. What came later is MATHEMATICAL, not data: (i) Nielsen 1999 made the single-copy exact statement a theorem (confirms, used here); (ii) irreversibility for mixed states (Vidal-Cirac 2001 as cited in 2111.02438; Lami-Regula 2021/23) showed that no general 'conservation' of entanglement exists -- which bears on the tree's WORDING, not on consumption; (iii) battery/catalysis frameworks (2405.10599) restore a conservation-like law only by enlarging the allowed operations beyond LOCC. Evidence either way: every piece of later literature read leaves 'exact teleportation of an unknown qubit through one ebit leaves zero shared entanglement, and LOCC cannot restore it' intact; none of it supports the word 'conservation' outside the asymptotic pure-state or battery settings. The physical premise that could fail is the LOCC restriction itself (a quantum channel between the parties would restore entanglement) -- that is a hypothesis of the theorem, not a datum.
grade_evidence: The theorem the tree needs stands and is re-derived here: exact (F = 1), deterministic teleportation of an arbitrary qubit through one pure ebit leaves the shared entanglement at exactly 0 on every outcome (sympy factorisation), exact teleportation requires the channel to be maximally entangled and consumes all of it (z3 over Nielsen's majorization theorem, unsat at residual dimensions 2-4, vacuity guard sat), and LOCC cannot make the resulting product state entangled again (Horodecki p.51; numeric). The declared constants 1.0/0.0 AGREE with the computation. It is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree uses it on a larger class than the sources support: (1) transit.py:27-28/:221-222 state 'you could not keep it open if you wanted to' without the exact-fidelity hypothesis -- computed, at F = 2/3 the pair survives intact -- and specthm.py:1186-1187 records that R11's fidelity is not yet fixed while binding CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE on it (specthm.py:1209); (2) transit.py drops the unknown-state hypothesis that specthm.py:1188-1190/:1212 keeps, and ledger.py M-S1A-P5 (:1357-1365) quotes the flag with no hypothesis; (3) 'one pair, one transit' holds per ebit, not per pair of arbitrary entanglement; (4) 'CONSERVATION LAW' is a misnomer -- the sources state non-increase; computed, cut entanglement goes 1 -> 0 for a pure input. Item (4) is a discrepancy of naming, not a refutation, and it does not change any flag's value. Nothing here is WRONG: no counterexample to any value the tree prints was found.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: transit.py/ledger.py stating the hypotheses (exact F = 1, unknown/arbitrary input, one pure ebit, LOCC only) wherever CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE is bound, and R11/M-S1A-P5 fixing the fidelity at 1 (or restating the consumption as a fidelity-dependent trade-off); renaming 'conservation law' to 'LOCC monotonicity (non-increase)'. To WRONG: an LOCC protocol that teleports an arbitrary qubit with fidelity exactly 1 through one ebit and leaves nonzero shared entanglement -- excluded here by the z3 check for pure residuals up to Schmidt dimension 4 and in general by Nielsen's theorem; for mixed residuals the Schmidt-number monotonicity argument is cited, not machine-checked here. To OPEN: none -- the sources were read and the finite claims checked.
